justification: B opens on a full photographic cover and holds one frame through the pages. A breaks the timeline across pages 2 and 3 and its page 3 starts with a stray tail; B page 3 leaves a void beside the picture.
A sets larger type with air and a confident overlay on the picture. B is cramped and small, with a picture stranded at the right of page 2, though A page 4 ends half empty.
The same layout page for page. A has a filled figure strip and B a ruled one plus a footer band; neither changes the reading.
B fits two well filled pages with clear section bands. A has larger figures but its last page is a small chart and a note with half the page unused.

B sets both languages side by side, puts two charts in one row and gives each statement a clean ledger. A stacks the languages, spends a page on one chart and strands a table at the top of page 5. The bars in B use several colours where one would do.
Both show a missing-glyph box in the figures row, so the comparison is excluded as defective.
Practically identical pages; only the height of the cover band differs.
B has a calm cover and a serif with room, suited to a paper. A squeezes everything and leaves one line on page 3, with References twice under a heavy band. B page 2 ends with a large gap.
Identical apart from the tinted current column in A, which helps the eye in the tables a little.
B has a real cover and generous bilingual heads. A is sound and compact with strong bands, but the document has no opening moment and its charts fill a page alone.
The same manual; A has thin running lines and B filled bands. The band gives identity and the thin line suits a manual; I cannot separate them.
A pairs the languages in columns and lays a panel on the picture. B sets the Arabic as small text under the English and ends on a half-used page.
The same decision paper; the figures differ slightly in weight only.
B has a strong title band and a filled figure strip, and reads as one designed set. A is cleaner and has more air but its white cover and even pages feel unfinished.
A has a full cover, a hero figure page and an opener with a contents strip, with real variation in pace. B is a dense run of the same banded page.
The same manual with filled bands in A and thin lines in B; the difference does not decide anything.
Identical pages; the tinted column in B gives the tables a slightly clearer reading line.
Identical but for the figures: the filled strip in B lifts them above the text better than the thin rules in A.

A has a photographic cover, a large pull quote and a full-width picture band, so the report has a pace. B is a plain logo cover and even pages. A ends on a mostly empty page 6 and carries tails onto pages 4 and 5.

B gives the first picture a full-width page moment and keeps text and picture apart. A lays dark panels on two similar small pictures, repeating itself, and page 3 opens with a stray picture. B page 4 opens awkwardly with the pull quote.
A composes two full pages with a picture panel and paired columns. B has larger bands but its last page is half used and its picture is small.
A has the stronger cover, a contents page and a hero figure, in a quiet serif. It leaves pages 3 and 4 half used. B is better filled, with panels on its pictures, so this is close.

B has a photographic cover, the languages in paired columns and both charts in one row. A has a white cover and gives a whole page to two large line charts. In B the table's title row sits under its column heads, which is wrong.
B keeps the figures with their section and fills four pages evenly. A strands the figures at the top of page 3 and leaves pages 3 and 5 half empty, though its overlay on page 4 is attractive.
B has a proper cover and pictures tied to their text. A ends on a page holding a lone picture and page 3 opens with a small stray one. The opening spread in A is strong, but the end falls apart.
B has a dark cover and a quiet serif that suits statements. A is efficient and well ordered but heavy, with bands everywhere.
The same decision paper; nothing separates the two pages.

B gives the Arabic readable size under strong section bands. A has larger pictures, but its Arabic is very small, the cover title breaks at the divider, and page 6 is half empty. B strands a table at the top of page 5.
Practically identical pages; only the height of the cover band differs.
A opens on a real dark cover and its quiet serif suits a feature. B starts straight into a band with heavy heads, and page 2 opens with a stray picture.

A holds the data in four composed pages of chart rows. B has a hero figure and openers but stretches thin content over eight pages, several of them mostly blank. In both, one-series bars change colour for no reason.
A shows a missing-glyph box inside the hero figure on page 2, so the comparison is excluded as defective.
A keeps the timeline whole and reads steadily. B has larger heads and a bigger picture, but its timeline breaks across pages 2 and 3.
A gives each section a page and fills the last page. B has the fuller picture band on page 3 but runs sections across pages and ends on a nearly empty page 6.
A's serif text and thin rules suit a short brief. B's sans and two heavy bands on page 2 are louder than two pages need, though its sections stand out more.

A has a photographic cover, languages in paired columns and two small charts in a row. B has a white cover and a page of two oversized line charts. The table title in A sits below the column heads, which needs fixing.
A has clear bands and a picture with a panel beside it, over three pages. B has a plain white cover, a chart alone on page 3 and a very tall picture on page 4. A page 3 is half used.
B gives sections their own pages and fills the last one. A has a strong picture band on page 3 but ends on a mostly empty page 6.
A has an opening band and picture panels with real presence. B is calm but repeats the same picture-then-text page, with lower halves unused and a plain cover.
B groups the charts in rows, gives the key figure a page and has a section opener. A gives each chart half a page for eight pages, with a plain cover. Bars in B change colour within one series.
A keeps sections moving over six full pages, with a bold cover and hero figure. B spends two whole pages on near-empty openers and leaves page 7 half blank.
B has a tinted picture cover, a good pull quote and a quiet serif. A is well filled and clear, and B page 4 is half empty, but A feels routine.
B sets the two languages in columns and gives the picture a large panel. A runs the languages in full-width lines with a small picture. A has a stronger figure strip.
A groups the charts into rows and has a cover, hero figure and opener. B gives each chart half a page over eight pages behind a plain cover. Bars in A change colour within one series.
The same structure. A's serif hero and thin running line feel more finished than B's sans and blue bands, but only slightly.
Identical but for the figures, where the filled strip in B stands out more than the plain row in A.
A has a dark cover and quiet serif, right for a manual, though page 5 holds only one table. B's drop caps are out of place in instructions, and a list item is stranded at the top of page 2.
The same brief; only the weight of a table rule differs.

Identical pages; the tinted column in B helps the tables a little.

A keeps the figures with their section and fits four even pages. B strands the figures on page 3 above a lone chart, though its panel on page 4 is attractive.
B reads comfortably at a larger size with quiet heads. A's bands are louder than a two-page paper needs and its text is small.
Identical apart from the first picture, a panel in A and a full-width band in B; both work, and both split the timeline.
Identical but for the figures, where the filled strip in A stands out more than the thin rules in B.
B's serif and thin rules give the paper more authority. A is clean but its numbered sans heads feel like a default.
A fits four pages with the panels doing the work. B's text is larger and its dark cover good, but it ends on a page with one lone picture.
A's dark cover and serif suit a manual. B's drop caps do not, and a list item is stranded on page 2. A page 5 is short.
A's numbered heads and full-width text read better in a short brief. B's drop cap sits oddly on a one-line paragraph and its text column is narrow.
